title: Prime-to-characteristic torsion kernels of smooth diagonalizable groups are finite and schematically dense
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $D$ be a smooth affine $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $D\simeq\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, where $F[M]$ has basis $e_m$, product $e_me_{m'}=e_{m+m'}$, comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$, and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Put $p=1$ in characteristic zero and $p=\operatorname{char}F$ otherwise. For each positive integer $n$ coprime to $p$, let $D[n]$ be the closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup, def-weil-closed-immersion] given on every commutative $F$-algebra $A$ by $D[n](A)=\{d\in D(A):d^n=1\}$. Then $D[n]$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}F$; the finite group $H_n=D[n](F)$ has positive order $c_n=|H_n|$ coprime to $p$. The family of closed immersions $D[n]\hookrightarrow D$ is schematically dense: every closed subscheme $Z\subseteq D$ through which all these immersions factor is $D$ itself. In particular, every regular function in $F[M]$ vanishing at all points of all $H_n$ is zero. No connectedness of $D$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5, printed pp.231–232 (finite kernels over an algebraically closed field); Theorem 12.32, printed p.242 (smooth-case schematic density); applied in Proposition 15.3, printed p.303. No Stacks tag for this diagonalizable-group theorem.

proof.text: By [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure], choose $M\simeq\mathbf Z^r\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^s\mathbf Z/d_i\mathbf Z$, with $d_i\geq1$; a finite direct sum is a finite product. By [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-group-geometric-criteria] this identifies $D$ as an $F$-group scheme with $\mathbf G_m^r\times\prod_i\mu_{d_i}$. In positive characteristic the same cited statement says smoothness excludes every nonzero element of $M$ annihilated by a power of $p$. If $p\mid d_i$, the class of $d_i/p$ in the $i$th cyclic factor is a nonzero element killed by $p$, a contradiction. Hence every $d_i$ is coprime to $p$; in characteristic zero this is automatic because $p=1$. Put $d=\prod_i d_i$, with empty product $1$. Then $d\geq1$ is coprime to $p$. All later constructions take place in this group-scheme product, so the chosen isomorphism preserves multiplication, kernels and their inclusions.

Fix $n\geq1$ coprime to $p$ and put $g_i=\gcd(d_i,n)$. The defining equations in [def-sc-gm-ga] show
$$D[n]=\mu_n^r\times\prod_i\mu_{g_i}.$$
Indeed for a unit $x$ in any commutative $F$-algebra, $x^{d_i}=x^n=1$ implies $x^{g_i}=1$: write $g_i=a d_i+b n$ with integers $a,b$ and use inverse powers. Conversely $g_i\mid d_i,n$ implies both equations. These are identities for arbitrary algebras, including nonreduced ones: the equations $x^{d_i}-1,x^n-1$ and $x^{g_i}-1$ generate the same ideal in $F[x,x^{-1}]$, since the quotient by the first two makes $x^{g_i}=1$, and each of the first two is a multiple of the third. Thus the displayed equality identifies the closed subgroup schemes and their inclusions, rather than only their $F$-points. The affine interpretation of these equations is [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Proposition 12.3 and the kernel calculation implicit in Theorem 12.32, printed pp.231–232,242; the Bezout calculation is elementary.

proof.text:
For each $a\in\{n,g_1,\ldots,g_s\}$, $a$ is invertible in $F$. Algebraic closedness [def-weil-algebraic-closure] splits $T^a-1$ by repeated removal of a linear factor. Apply [lem-sfb-split-binomial-root-torsor] with its exponent set to $a$ and its binomial constant and chosen root both set to $1$. Its cardinality assertion and final factorization give $a$ distinct roots and
$$T^a-1=\prod_{\zeta\in\mu_a(F)}(T-\zeta).$$
For distinct roots, $(T-\zeta)$ and $(T-\eta)$ are comaximal because their difference is the nonzero scalar $\eta-\zeta$. Their intersection equals their product: for comaximal $I,J$, $x\in I\cap J$ and $1=i+j$ give $x=xi+xj\in IJ$; a product of ideals comaximal with $J$ is comaximal with $J$ by multiplying the expressions for $1$. Induction handles the finite family. Therefore [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] identifies $F[T]/(T^a-1)$ with $F^{\mu_a(F)}$ by evaluations. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] to obtain $\mu_a\simeq\coprod_{\mu_a(F)}\operatorname{Spec}F$. Taking the finite products in step 2 yields a disjoint union indexed by $\mu_n(F)^r\times\prod_i\mu_{g_i}(F)$: on coordinate algebras [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the tensor of $F^E$ and $F^{E'}$ is $F^{E\times E'}$, via $x\otimes y\mapsto(x_e y_f)_{e,f}$, with inverse $z\mapsto\sum_{e,f}z_{e,f}\delta_e\otimes\delta_f$, where $\delta_e$ is the coordinate idempotent. These maps are multiplicative and inverse on the idempotents, whose sums are $1$; their algebra-map construction uses [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Consequently
$$c_n=|D[n](F)|=n^r\prod_i g_i\geq1,$$
which is coprime to $p$. This proves the finite-kernel and order assertions, including $n=1$.

source.place: Proposition 12.3, Remark 12.5 and Theorem 12.32, printed pp.231–232,242; CRT: Stacks Tag 00DT, algebra.tex, lemma-chinese-remainder.

proof.text:
Write $N=\prod_i\mu_{d_i}$ and
$$B=F[u_1,\ldots,u_s]/(u_i^{d_i}-1)_i,\qquad L=B[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}].$$
For $s=0$ set $B=F$. Here $L$ means the algebra of finite sums $\sum_{v\in\mathbf Z^r}b_vt^v$ with coefficientwise addition and $t^vt^w=t^{v+w}$. The product presentation of step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identify $F[M]$ with $L$: the cyclic basis elements give the bounded powers of the $u_i$, while the free basis elements give $t^v$. Whenever $d\mid n$, every $u_i$ already has $n$th power $1$, so step 2 identifies $D[n]\hookrightarrow D$ with the quotient
$$q_n:L\longrightarrow L/J_n,\qquad J_n=(t_1^n-1,\ldots,t_r^n-1).$$
There is a $B$-algebra identification $L/J_n=B[t_1,\ldots,t_r]/(t_j^n-1)_j$: the variables on the right are units with inverses $t_j^{n-1}$, giving inverse maps on the displayed generators. Successive applications of [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], with the previously adjoined variables as coefficient ring, give a free $B$-basis
$$\{t^v:0\leq v_j<n\text{ for all }j\}$$
for this quotient. Thus a polynomial in that exponent box maps to zero only if every $B$-coefficient is zero. For $r=0$, $L=B$, $J_n=0$ and the basis consists of $1$.

source.place: Theorem 12.33, printed p.243: explicit coordinate quotient for multiples of the finite-factor order, with the monic-quotient basis spelling out its joint-injectivity argument.

proof.text: Let $f\in L$ have $q_n(f)=0$ for every positive $n$ coprime to $p$ and divisible by $d$ (the $n$ for which step 4 identifies $q_n$ with restriction to $D[n]$). If $f\ne0$, its Laurent support is finite and nonempty. Choose $n=d(1+kp)$ with $k\geq0$ large enough that $n$ exceeds the difference between the largest and smallest exponent of this support in every free coordinate. Such $n$ are unbounded, divisible by $d$, and coprime to $p$ (also when $p=1$). Multiplying $f$ by the monomial whose exponents are the negatives of these coordinate minima puts its support in the box $0\leq v_j<n$, preserving a nonzero coefficient. Its image under $q_n$ is still zero, contrary to the free $B$-basis of step 4. Hence $f=0$. For $r=0$ there are no coordinate bounds and $q_n$ is already the identity. This proves joint injectivity using only prime-to-$p$ multiples of $d$; no inference from the unrestricted family of all integers is needed.

source.place: Theorems 12.32–12.33, printed pp.242–243: finite-support completion of the coordinate argument, restricted to prime-to-characteristic multiples.

proof.text: If $Z\subseteq D=\operatorname{Spec}L$ is closed, [def-weil-closed-immersion] writes it as $\operatorname{Spec}(L/I)$ over $D$. If every $D[n]\hookrightarrow D$ factors through $Z$, then by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the coordinate map $L\to\mathcal O(D[n])$ factors through $L/I$, so it annihilates $I$; for $n$ coprime to $p$ and divisible by $d$ this map is $q_n$ by step 4. Step 5 gives $I=0$, whence $Z=D$. Finally, by the evaluation identifications in step 3, $\mathcal O(D[n])=F^{H_n}$ and the restriction of a regular function has coordinates its values at the points of $H_n$. If all those values vanish for every allowed $n$, its restriction to every $D[n]$ is zero, in particular its image under $q_n$ is zero whenever $d\mid n$, and step 5 makes the function zero. The proof treats all finite factors of $D$ and never assumes connectedness.

source.place: Theorem 12.32, printed p.242; affine ideal formulation and the reduced finite kernels of Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5.

Statement unchanged, no new nodes, no SGA, no tool_uses. Step 1: lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure plus the diagonalizable geometric criteria; smoothness rules out p | d_i. Step 2: Bezout gives an ideal equality, so D[n] = μ_n^r × ∏μ_{gcd(d_i,n)} as schemes. Step 3: split-binomial with a=α=1, CRT with an inline proof that intersection = product, the coproduct spectrum and the tensor of finite products give c_n = n^r ∏g_i, prime to p. Step 4: L = B[t^±] and O(D[n]) = L/J_n for d | n; repeated monic-quotient freeness gives a box basis (Milne 12.33). Step 5: n = d(1+kp) plus a support shift gives joint injectivity. Step 6: the affine closed-immersion argument gives I = 0, hence density and the pointwise test. Small cases checked: M=0, μ_2 in char 3, G_m×μ_3 in char 7, r=0. One repair, to proof text only: step 5 assumed q_n(f)=0 for every n prime to p, but step 6 only supplies it for d | n, the only n where q_n is the restriction to D[n] (for d ∤ n, O(D[n]) = L/(J_n+(u^n−1))). Steps 5 and 6 now restrict to n prime to p with d | n, which is all the argument uses. Not a duplicate: lem-sfb-torus-torsion-joint-injectivity covers all n, not the prime-to-p family. lean.statement: theorem smooth_diagonal_primeToTorsion_density (F : Type u) [Field F] [IsAlgClosed F] (D : Grp (Over (Spec (.of F)))) [IsAffine D.X.left] [Smooth D.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType D.X.hom] [QuasiCompact D.X.hom] (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [AddGroup.FG M] (e : D ≅ diagonalizableGroup F M) : (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → n.Coprime (ringExpChar F) → ∃ c : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ c.Coprime (ringExpChar F) ∧ Nat.card (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of F))) ⟶ torsionSubgroupScheme D.X n) = c ∧ Nonempty (torsionSubgroupScheme D.X n ≅ ∐ fun _ : Fin c ↦ 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of F))))) ∧ (∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (i : Z ⟶ D.X.left), IsClosedImmersion i → (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → n.Coprime (ringExpChar F) → ∃ j : (torsionSubgroupScheme D.X n).left ⟶ Z, j ≫ i = (torsionSubgroupScheme.ι D.X n).left) → IsIso i) ∧ (∀ f : AddMonoidAlgebra F M, (∀ n : ℕ, 0 < n → n.Coprime (ringExpChar F) → ∀ x : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of F))) ⟶ torsionSubgroupScheme D.X n, (Spec.preimage (x.left ≫ (torsionSubgroupScheme.ι D.X n).left ≫ e.hom.hom.hom.left)).hom f = 0) → f = 0)
